## Japan FIFA World Cup 2026 Group Stage Fixtures and Key Players Under Hajime Moriyasu
[...]
Japan are expected to stick with the three-man defense.

Germany and Spain
[...]
Moriyasu has shown flexibility between a back four and a back three, often shifting in-game. Japan press high, transition quickly and rely on the technical quality of their wide attackers to break lines. Endo’s screening role is central to their structure. Against stronger sides they may sit deeper and counter — exactly the blueprint that toppled Germany and Spain in 2022. Set-piece organisation and game intelligence are hallmarks.
[...]
Projected finish
[...]
Group F runners-up contender — Round of 16, with quarter-final upside if the draw opens up.
[...]
Japan are good enough to escape Group F but face a fight against the Netherlands and Sweden. We expect a tight battle for second place; if Kubo and Doan stay healthy, Japan can reach the Round of 16 again. Breaking into the quarter-finals would be historic and is within reach if the draw opens up.

Expect Haiti to set up pragmatically: a compact, disciplined defensive block designed to frustrate superior opponents, with quick, direct counter-attacks aimed at their physical strikers (Pierrot, Nazon). Migné’s side will likely prioritise organisation, low-block resilience and set-piece threat, looking to turn moments of individual quality and transition speed into rare but dangerous chances.
[...]
Projected finish
[...]
Group-stage exit — but a goal on the World Cup stage and a nation united in pride.
[...]
Haiti are likely to finish bottom of Group C against this calibre of opposition. But in an expanded, unpredictable format, a hard-fought draw or a shock result is not impossible. Realistic success looks like a competitive showing, a goal on the World Cup stage and a nation united in pride — regardless of the points.
